scope: F131 exhibit — independent recomputation of the window census
source: results/window_rescue_c5075.json (the ORIGINAL C5075 census, pre-C6629 recovery)
ratio_definition_recovered: device_readout.MEAN / used_readout.MEDIAN. Not stated in the row; recovered from the F125 worked example (used median 0.00403 vs device mean 0.03075 = 7.63x). A first pass using device MEDIAN gives 1.75x on the sample record and reproduces nothing — the definition matters and was not written down.

recomputed_counts.reconciliation: DONE 116 minus per-qubit-present 112 = 4 — EXACTLY the four retrievable-but-per-qubit-missing windows the C6629 update recovered. The GONE count (58) matches the ledger exactly.

DISCREPANCY_FOUND: The artifact holds 116 retrievable and 174 total where the ledger states 115 and 173 — each EXACTLY ONE over. The gone count matches to the unit, and the four-window recovery reconciles, so the residual is a single record. CAUSE NOT DETERMINED and deliberately not guessed: it could be a job cited by two findings counted once in the row, or an entry that is not a distinct cited window. Recording the exact artifact figures so the row can be reconciled by whoever owns the citation list.
verdict_on_the_finding: The HEADLINE SURVIVES INTACT. >2x at 97%, >4x at 54% and the 64.9x worst case reproduce EXACTLY; the median computes 4.38x against a stated 4.3x. The claim that a device-wide aggregate overstates a flights own readout noise several-fold is confirmed, and the one-record count difference does not touch it.
verdict: EXHIBIT COMPLETE with one unreconciled record. EXHIBIT, not a ratification.
exhibit_self_defect_recorded: First write of this exhibit used the dict key "ledger_says" TWICE in one literal; Python silently kept the last and DROPPED the ledger comparison for n_windows (111). A duplicate key in a dict literal is silent data loss with no error and no warning — found only by reading the emitted JSON back. Recorded here rather than quietly corrected, because an exhibit that hides its own repair is not an exhibit.
